title: A lazy log pipeline with three generators
problem: Write three generator functions in logpipe.py that can be chained into a pipeline: parse_lines turns raw log lines into (LEVEL, message) tuples, only_level keeps one level, and first_n stops after n items. The pipeline must stay lazy: it must work on an endless input and must not read more lines than it needs.
requirements: All three functions are generator functions (they use yield and return nothing)
parse_lines strips each line, skips blank lines and lines starting with '#', and yields (LEVEL, message): the first word uppercased, and the rest of the line (stripped, or '' if there is none)
only_level yields the records whose level equals the given level, compared case-insensitively
first_n yields at most n items and never pulls item n+1 from its input; n <= 0 pulls nothing
No lists of the whole input: each stage handles one item at a time
contract:
parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]
only_level(records: Iterable[tuple[str, str]], level: str) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]
first_n(items: Iterable[T], n: int) -> Iterator[T]
expectedBehavior: list(parse_lines(['  warn  disk 91%  ', '', '# x', 'DEBUG'])) == [('WARN', 'disk 91%'), ('DEBUG', '')]; list(first_n(itertools.count(), 3)) == [0, 1, 2], even though count() never ends
edgeCases: Blank and whitespace-only lines, comment lines
Lines from a file still end in '\n'
n larger than the input, n == 0, negative n
An endless input (the tests fail a stage that pulls far more items than it needs)
first_n must leave item n+1 unread in the source iterator
hints: Conceptual: each function is a loop over its input that yields instead of appending to a list. A stage only runs when the stage after it asks for the next item, so nothing may build the whole result first.

Specific: for parse_lines, strip first, then decide to skip, then split the line into at most two parts (split has a maxsplit parameter). For first_n, think about the order: if you check the count before yielding, you have already pulled one item too many.
Implementation: first_n: return immediately if n <= 0; otherwise loop over items, yield the item, add 1 to a counter, and return as soon as the counter reaches n.
evaluation: Each function is a generator; no list of the whole input is built
first_n stops pulling at exactly n items
Edge cases are handled by the logic, not by special-casing test inputs
